record.original_question: Let the function f have the power series f (z) = ∞ n n=0 an z of radius of convergence 1; let E be the singular set on T, and suppose that N X sup sup an ξ < ∞. ξ∈E N ≥0 n=0 It hasPbeen shown by Allan, O’Farrell and Ransford [19] that, if E has measure zero, then ∞ n n=0 an z converges to f (z) at each point z in T \ E. Does the conclusion remain true if E has positive measure? (Nothing appears to be known either way.) (T. J. Ransford)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ and $\mathbb{T}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|=1\}$. Let $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic with power series $f(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n z^n$ of radius of convergence equal to $1$. Recall that a point $\zeta\in\mathbb{T}$ is called a regular point of $f$ if $f$ extends holomorphically to a neighborhood of $\zeta$; the singular set $E\subset\mathbb{T}$ is the complement in $\mathbb{T}$ of the set of regular points. Assume that
$$\sup_{\zeta\in E}\,\sup_{N\ge 0}\left|\sum_{n=0}^{N} a_n \zeta^n\right| < \infty.$$
It is known that if $E$ has Lebesgue measure zero on $\mathbb{T}$, then the partial sums $\sum_{n=0}^{N} a_n z^n$ converge to $f(z)$ for every $z\in\mathbb{T}\setminus E$.

Question: Does the same conclusion hold without the assumption that $E$ has measure zero — that is, whenever the above uniform boundedness condition holds, must $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n z^n$ converge to $f(z)$ at every $z\in\mathbb{T}\setminus E$, even when $E$ has positive Lebesgue measure?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any published resolution of this question. The problem is stated as open with "nothing appears to be known either way," and no later work was found that settles the case of singular sets of positive measure.

status_evidence.title: Some developments around the Katznelson–Tzafriri theorem (arXiv:2204.13411)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses results of Allan, O'Farrell and Ransford in operator-theoretic context related to convergence and measure-zero sets.
status_evidence.claim: Allan–O'Farrell–Ransford's result is referenced in connection with measure-zero hypotheses; no extension to the positive-measure case is reported.
